ART CAMP 2026 · A DAY IN COLOURNº 01
The Presentation

HIS LIFE IN A PENCIL LINE

The day began with a presentation that went beyond simply teaching art. Sir Melvin Raj CR shared experiences from his journey, spoke about what artists encounter, and introduced the students to techniques and ways of looking at art through his own perspective.

MELVIN RAJ CR · ASSISTANT PROFESSOR, GEC
the story begins…
ART CAMP 2026 · A DAY IN COLOURNº 02
The Classroom

ASK. LISTEN. INTERACT.

Around him, the room leaned in. Questions came slowly at first, then freely — about lines, about patience, about what a drawing owes to the person looking at it. Sir listened as much as he spoke, and the classroom became a conversation.

ART CAMP 2026 · A DAY IN COLOURNº 03
Practical Session · 01

TOOLS BEFORE THE CANVAS

The session moved from talk to making. Pencil colours and oil pastels changed hands, paper was squared up, and every desk slowly turned into a small studio — before a single line was drawn.

  • graphite pencils
  • pencil colours
  • oil pastels
  • an eraser
ready when you are
ART CAMP 2026 · A DAY IN COLOURNº 04
Exercise Nº 1

THE FIRST MARK

Every artist in the room began the same way: one square, one pencil, and the fundamentals of shading. Light pressure, patient layers — a small exercise that quietly opened the whole day.

start small
ART CAMP 2026 · A DAY IN COLOURNº 05
Tea Break

A LITTLE TEA, A LOT OF COLOUR

Between exercises, the room stepped out for tea — steam, sugar, and a few quiet minutes before colour took over the rest of the day.

ART CAMP 2026 · A DAY IN COLOURNº 06
Oil Pastels

COLOUR IN PROGRESS

Then came colour. Two oil pastels side by side, learning to merge — blended with a fingertip, softened with a tissue, nudged along with an earbud, exactly as sir showed them. Simple techniques, and the paper filled with gradients.

BLEND · SOFTEN · NUDGE
ART CAMP 2026 · A DAY IN COLOURNº 07
Margin Notes

NEW TRICKS, NEW WAYS

The camp was never only about finishing a drawing. Between exercises, sir passed around small techniques — a different grip, a softer edge, a smudge made on purpose — and the students collected them like notes in a margin.

blend with a fingertip
soften with a tissue
nudge colour with an earbud
NEXT — FROM SHAPES TO TREES
Exercise Nº 2

FROM SHAPES TO TREES

The lesson grew out of simple forms into something alive. A trunk in brown, a crown built up in greens — shading and blending, now with a subject. The morning's squares had become a tree.

same pencil, new idea
ART CAMP 2026 · A DAY IN COLOURNº 09
1:30
Intermission

Lunch.

AFTER LUNCH · BACK AROUND 1:30 PM
The Afternoon Session

THE AFTERNOON BEGINS

Before the main artwork of the afternoon, sir demonstrated a small scenery in yellow, orange and black — the same warmth that opens this album's cover. The students watched a sky go down in three colours.

THE DEMONSTRATION PALETTE
ART CAMP 2026 · A DAY IN COLOURNº 11
The Main Exercise

A LITTLE PEACOCK

The afternoon's main exercise: a peacock, drawn from a reference on a phone, oil pastel on a gridded page.

DARK BLUE · BLACK · LIGHT BLUE · DARK GREEN · LIGHT GREEN · YELLOW
ART CAMP 2026 · A DAY IN COLOURNº 12
Work in Progress

FROM REFERENCE TO OUR OWN

The grid did its work. What began as a copied reference slowly turned into each student's own bird — the same pose, different wings, colours chosen one pastel at a time.

almost there…
ART CAMP 2026 · A DAY IN COLOURNº 13
The Camp's Own Gallery

MADE BY US

Every peacock in this room was drawn that afternoon — different hands, different greens and blues. No names, no rankings. Just work made by us.

STUDENT WORKS FROM THE CAMP · OIL PASTEL ON PAPER
The Lighter Side

BETWEEN THE BRUSHSTROKES

Between the artworks were the in-between moments — a pastel passed along a row, a glance at someone else's paper, laughter that had nothing to do with the drawings. The camp's quiet, smiling middle.

ART CAMP 2026 · A DAY IN COLOURNº 15
The Butterfly Activity

EVERYONE GETS A CANVAS

The nannies and ayyas of the campus were invited to draw too. Each was given an oil pastel set, and for a while the classroom held two kinds of students at once — both beginners, both absorbed.

butterflies, in progress
ART CAMP 2026 · A DAY IN COLOURNº 16
Their Butterflies

A FIRST TOUCH OF COLOUR AGAIN

For the nannies and ayyas, the butterfly page was a return — a first touch of colour since their school days. They stood with their drawings the way the students did: proud, and a little surprised that colour had been waiting all along.

ART CAMP 2026 · A DAY IN COLOURNº 17
The Camp, Complete

ONE FRAME. EVERYONE.

One day. Many colours. One shared memory.
